provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: The sun and energy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state that the sun gives light and heat.
The pupils should be able to list two ways to stay safe in the sun.

Introduction:
We see the sun every day. It gives us light and heat.

Content:
The sun is a big star in the sky. It lights our day. It warms our earth. The sun gives us energy to play. When we play in the sun, we must wear our hats. We must drink water. Water helps us not to be too hot.

Class activity:
Let us all go outside. We will trace our shadows on the ground. We will see how our shadows look.

Evaluation questions:
What does the sun give us?
Name one thing we do to stay safe in the sun.
Is the sun hot or cold?

Summary:
The sun gives light and heat. We must stay safe in the sun.

topics.title: Shadows through the day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain that shadows change position.
The pupils should be able to identify their shadow at different times.

Introduction:
Yesterday we traced our shadows. Shadows are made by the sun.

Content:
A shadow is a dark shape. The sun makes shadows. Shadows move when the sun moves. In the morning, shadows are long. At noon, shadows are short. Shadows are on the opposite side of the sun. Our bodies make shadows too.

Class activity:
We will trace our shadow at morning. We will trace it again at noon. We will see how it moves.

Evaluation questions:
What makes a shadow?
When is a shadow long?
What happens to shadows when the sun moves?

Summary:
Shadows change position during the day.

topics.title: Light sources
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list three sources of light.
The pupils should be able to sort objects into light or dark.

Introduction:
We need light to see. Some things make light.

Content:
Light helps us see. The sun is a light source. A torch is a light source. A lamp is a light source. A candle is a light source. Some things do not make light. We call them dark. We can sort things into light or dark.

Class activity:
We will have many objects. We will sort them into light sources and dark objects.

Evaluation questions:
Name one light source.
Is the sun a light source?
What do we call things that do not make light?

Summary:
The sun, torch, lamp and candle are light sources.

topics.title: Sound makers
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify three sound makers.
The pupils should be able to sort sounds into loud or soft.

Introduction:
We hear sounds every day. Some things make sounds.

Content:
A sound is what we hear. A drum makes a loud sound. A bell makes a ringing sound. A whistle makes a high sound. Some sounds are loud. Some sounds are soft. We can sort sounds into loud or soft.

Class activity:
We will play a drum. We will ring a bell. We will blow a whistle. We will sort them into loud or soft.

Evaluation questions:
What does a drum make?
Is a bell loud or soft?
How many sounds can you name?

Summary:
Drums, bells and whistles make sounds. Sounds can be loud or soft.

topics.title: Hot and cold things
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify hot and cold things.
The pupils should be able to sort pictures into hot or cold.

Introduction:
Some things feel hot. Some things feel cold.

Content:
The sun is hot. Fire is hot. Ice is cold. Water from the fridge is cold. We use our sense of touch to feel hot and cold. Hot things make us warm. Cold things make us cool. We can sort things into hot or cold.

Class activity:
We will have pictures of hot and cold things. We will sort them into two groups.

Evaluation questions:
Is the sun hot or cold?
What is cold?
Can you name something hot?

Summary:
The sun is hot. Ice is cold. We can sort things by temperature.

topics.title: Melting and freezing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what happens when ice melts.
The pupils should be able to explain what happens when water freezes.

Introduction:
Ice and water are the same but different.

Content:
Ice is frozen water. When ice is in the sun, it melts. Melting means ice turns into water. When water is very cold, it freezes. Freezing means water turns into ice. We see melting when we hold ice in our hand. We see freezing when we put water in the freezer.

Class activity:
We will put ice in a bowl. We will watch it melt. We will put water in the freezer and watch it freeze.

Evaluation questions:
What happens to ice in the sun?
What is freezing?
What does melting mean?

Summary:
Ice melts in the sun. Water freezes when it is very cold.

topics.title: Machines around us
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list three machines.
The pupils should be able to explain that machines make work easy.

Introduction:
We use machines every day. Machines help us.

Content:
A machine is a thing that helps us work. A fan is a machine. It makes us cool. A blender is a machine. It helps us make juice. A car is a machine. It helps us go fast. Machines make work easy for us.

Class activity:
We will pretend to be machines. We will show how a fan works. We will show how a car works.

Evaluation questions:
Name one machine.
How does a fan help us?
Do machines make work easy?

Summary:
Fans, blenders and cars are machines. Machines make work easy.

topics.title: Wheels and ramps
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate how wheels move.
The pupils should be able to compare steep and gentle ramps.

Introduction:
We see wheels and ramps every day. They help things move.

Content:
A wheel is round. It rolls. A ramp is a slope. We use ramps to move things up or down. A steep ramp is very sloped. A gentle ramp is not very sloped. Cars go faster down a steep ramp. Cars go slower down a gentle ramp.

Class activity:
We will roll cars down a ramp. We will try a steep ramp and a gentle ramp. We will see which is faster.

Evaluation questions:
What shape is a wheel?
What is a ramp?
Which ramp makes cars go faster?

Summary:
Wheels roll. Ramps help things move. Steep ramps are faster.

topics.title: Building and balancing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to build a tall tower.
The pupils should be able to balance a scale with blocks.

Introduction:
We can build things. We can balance things.

Content:
Building means making something tall with blocks. Balancing means making things equal. When we build a tower, we put blocks on top of each other. When we balance a scale, we put the same weight on both sides. If the scale tips, it is not balanced.

Class activity:
We will build towers with blocks. We will balance scales with blocks.

Evaluation questions:
What is building?
What does balancing mean?
How do you make a tower not fall?

Summary:
We build towers with blocks. We balance scales to make them equal.

topics.title: Revision and inventors day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to show a machine or tower.
The pupils should be able to talk like a scientist.

Introduction:
We learned about machines and building. Today we show what we made.

Content:
Today we will show our machines or towers. We will talk about what we made. We will use big words like force and balance. We will pretend to be scientists. Scientists discover new things.

Class activity:
Each pupil will show their machine or tower. They will explain how it works.

Evaluation questions:
What machine did you make?
How does your tower stand up?
What is one thing scientists do?

Summary:
We showed our machines and towers. We talked like scientists.
